units.content: Architecture repeats O→E→U→𝒰→𝒞→π→Y and repair Y−Ŷ→Q→L→ΔL→Y′.
Architecture is explicitly a causal proposal; each layer predicts a distinct intervention under controlled failure.
Interface failure is O(x_a)=O(x_b) while reliable action requires π*(x_a)≠π*(x_b); optimization over O cannot recover the missing distinction.
Evidence includes provenance, measurement conditions, uncertainty and identification limits; it can support prediction without mechanism or local performance without universal transfer.
Authority-bearing update schema includes content, evidence/provenance/independence, scope, confidence, dependencies, authorized actions, retest, reopening and history.
Update ecology contains active, dormant, suspended, defeated, superseded and archived updates and supports merge, split, consolidate, narrow, suspend, supersede, retire and reopen.
Conflicts may arise from factual disagreement, objectives, environmental shift, resources, hidden context or governance failure; conflict does not imply one update is false.
Constitution computes situated priority ρ_i=𝒞(U_i,context,time,goal,stakes,ecology), not confidence ranking alone.
Constitutional operations are Activate, Admit, Arbitrate, Aggregate, Suspend, Explore, Retire and Appeal.
Challenge channels should have relevant independence from the pathway evaluated; practical independence is dimension-specific rather than absolute.
Valid challenge should yield bounded revision, whereas pseudo-challenge should trigger inspection without capture.
Use shallowest sufficient locus across Observation→Inference→Mechanism→Representation→Interface→Governance, allowing coupled causes when evidence pathways may be compromised.
Frozen benchmark groups interventions as ΔU update, Δ𝒞 constitutional, ΔO interface and ΔQ challenge.
Authority acquisition changes weighting or operational authority of claims, policies, representations or experiments.
State incorporation places an update into accessible parameters, memory, retrieval, rules, tools, attention or experiment selection.
Behavioral realization requires incorporated state to cause a future counterfactual policy difference after corrective cues are removed.
Adaptive governance appropriately preserves, modifies, suspends or retires acquired updates as evidence and conditions change.
Architecture document specifies objects and predicted intervention roles; it contains no executed causal discrimination result.
Benchmark objective is causal failure localization plus smallest sufficient revision, not immediate output correction alone.
Central prospective comparison is governed correction versus content-only correction under later removal, delay, transfer, shift and conflict.
Update failure: stored update false, stale or mis-scoped; expected ΔU.
Constitutional failure: accurate updates but activation/evidence weighting/arbitration systematically selects incorrectly; expected Δ𝒞.
Interface failure: reliable decision depends on unavailable distinction; expected ΔO.
Challenge failure: defect cannot be exposed, correlated evidence is misread as independent, or pseudo-challenge captures governance; expected ΔQ.
Same visible symptom must arise from different hidden generators so classification cannot rely on superficial cues.
Protocol begins with baseline, scoped/provenance-bearing correction, then removes correction wording/evaluator cues/original examples.
Protocol then tests delay, near/structural/far transfer, and boundary cases where the update must not apply.
Later phases introduce conflict, environmental shift, defeating evidence/reversal, and valid independent challenge paired with pseudo-challenge.
Failure-localization accuracy is P(predicted locus=true generating locus).
Revision sufficiency is held-out removal of the generating failure.
Revision locality and retention measure preservation of unaffected behavior/structure and persistence after feedback removal/delay.
Scoped transfer and boundary preservation test improvement within identified structure and stability outside evidence-supported scope.
Reversibility tests narrowing/suspension/supersession/retirement; challenge selectivity is sensitivity to valid challenge minus sensitivity to pseudo-challenge.
Governance efficiency compares reliability gain to arbitration cost, representation burden and constitutional debt.
Minimize revision cost subject to held-out reliability/retention lower bounds, spillover/latency tolerances and preserved reopening.

Prospective baselines include in-context-only correction, persistent unstructured memory, ungovened rule accumulation, fixed-priority arbitration, context-sensitive arbitration without constitutional revision, and full governed architecture.

Authority should fall if simpler systems match localization/recovery, governance envelopes fail retention/scope/reversal, constitutional revision spills over, challenge selection fails, governance cost dominates, simpler representations suffice, or internal labels predict explanation rather than recovery.
Support raises confidence, represented failure receives local revision, and only break—an empirically necessary unrepresentable distinction—licenses architectural expansion.
Validated outcome≠validated mechanism; correct prediction≠universal authority; successful intervention≠unrestricted policy control.
Active updates should carry content, evidence, provenance/independence, scope, confidence, dependencies, authorized actions, retest, reopening/expiration and revision history.
Lifecycle states include proposed, admitted, active, consolidated, narrowed, suspended, split, merged, superseded, retired, reopened and archived; authority removal need not erase lineage.
Priority is situated through ρ_i=𝒞(U_i,x,t,goal,stakes,𝒰), considering context fit, evidence, dependencies, recency, risk, reversibility, objectives and resources.
Conflict taxonomy distinguishes conditional, evidential, policy, temporal, resource and governance conflicts with different diagnostic responses.
No constitutional rule may be sole judge of evidence against itself; challenge independence should match the implicated failure dimension.
Raw objection does not directly amend the constitution; it may earn inspection, retest, suspension, exploration or bounded revision.
Mature governance combines permeability to discriminating consequence with integrity against noise, correlation, manipulation and capture.
Debt vector includes conflict, stale-authority, dependency, revision-latency, opacity, challenge (source typo 'challene') and complexity debt.
Governance capacity must scale with update-interaction complexity.
No rule is sole judge against itself; no component permanently disables all appeal; challenge may force inspection without dictating replacement.
Constitutional changes preserve provenance/reversibility where feasible; repeated unexplained consequence may escalate; challenge channels remain auditable and replaceable.
